blocks.en: The farmers with the least land, the least capital buffer, and often the least physical capacity to adapt are disproportionately the ones farming in Taiwan’s most volatile microclimates.

blocks.en: In Taiwan, 99.2% of farms are small-scale (under 2 hectares), together managing 85.3% of the island's agricultural land, yet many of these farmers face growing climate challenges with limited resources to respond. Through geospatial analysis, we mapped climate patterns, farmland distribution, and socioeconomic conditions to understand where these challenges are most severe. We also connected our findings with farmer interviews and field visits to better understand the people behind the data. By identifying communities where climate risks and limited resources overlap, our analysis helps us understand where ReLEAF could make the greatest difference, bringing plant protection closer to the farmers who need it most.

blocks.en: Introduction

blocks.zh: 前言

blocks.en: In Taiwan, 99.2% of farms are small-scale (under 2 hectares), yet together they work 85.3% of the island's farmed land, on terrain where a single region can span a temperature range rivaling the distance between Miami and Anchorage. ReLEAF is built for the shape Taiwan actually has.

blocks.zh: 臺灣有 99.2% 的農場屬於小規模（2 公頃以下），卻合計耕作全島 85.3% 的農地；而在這樣的地形上，單一地區內的溫差幅度足以媲美邁阿密到安克拉治之間的差距。ReLEAF 是為臺灣真實的樣貌而打造的。

blocks.en: Single interviews cannot establish whether what one farmer describes is an isolated hardship or a structural pattern. Answering this requires working at a different scale entirely: parcel-level land records, station-level climate data, and demographic surveys, aggregated across all counties rather than gathered farm by farm. This is where the role of geospatial analysis comes in, complementary to case studies.

blocks.zh: 單一訪談無法判定一位農友所描述的困境是個別遭遇，還是結構性的型態。要回答這個問題，必須換到完全不同的尺度：地塊層級的土地紀錄、測站層級的氣候數據，以及人口調查，並以全部縣市為範圍彙整，而不是一場農場一場農場地蒐集。這就是地理空間分析的角色，與個案研究互補。

blocks.en: Existing geospatial studies of Taiwanese agriculture tend to treat variables in isolation: climate-trend analyses map warming or rainfall change without reference to who farms the affected land, while agricultural demographic surveys report vulnerability without a spatial climate layer to test it against. None, to our knowledge, overlay farmland fragmentation, climate volatility, and a documented crop-stress yield effect at the parcel or township level simultaneously. This page presents our method and findings.

blocks.zh: 既有的臺灣農業地理空間研究傾向把變數分開處理：氣候趨勢分析繪出暖化或降雨變化，卻不交代受影響的土地是誰在耕作；農業人口調查報告脆弱度，卻沒有一層空間氣候資料可以對照檢驗。就我們所知，還沒有研究在地塊或鄉鎮層級同時疊合農地破碎化、氣候波動度，以及有文獻記錄的作物逆境產量效應。本頁說明我們的方法與發現。

blocks.en: Beyond layering maps, geospatial analysis feeds the math model’s simulations for the business plan; it is checked against wet lab's own stress-response data, so the map's "who needs this" and the bench's "does this work" can answer each other; and it's cross-referenced against Human Practices' direct farmer interviews, so the pattern in the data is tested against what people are actually living through.

blocks.en: Rice is the primary calorie source for more than half the world's population (FAO, 2004), and across Asia it is grown at every scale — from smallholder plots to industrial acreage — as both a staple food and an economic backbone. The most dangerous part of this dependency is not the stress a farmer can see coming; it is the stress that arrives when no one is in the field to see it—during night time.
blocks.text: Rice is the primary calorie source for more than half the world's population (FAO, 2004), and across Asia it is grown at every scale — from smallholder plots to industrial acreage — as both a staple food and an economic backbone. The most dangerous part of this dependency is not the stress a farmer can see coming; it is the stress that arrives when no one is in the field to see it—during night time.
blocks.zh: 稻米是全球超過半數人口的主要熱量來源（FAO, 2004），在亞洲各種規模的農地上都有人種——從小農的田塊到工業化的大面積農地——既是主食，也是經濟的骨幹。這份依賴最危險的地方，不是農友看得出來即將到來的逆境，而是沒有人在田裡看得見時才降臨的逆境——在夜間。

blocks.en: Farming has always been a practice of response: a farmer notices wilting, discoloration, or dry soil, and intervenes. That model assumes stress leaves a visible trace in time to act on. Rising nighttime temperatures break that assumption. A 25-year record from the International Rice Research Institute’s farm in the Philippines (Peng et al., 2004) showed that from 1979 to 2003, nighttime minimum temperatures rose roughly three times faster than daytime maximums, and that dry-season grain yield fell by about 10% for every 1°C rise in nighttime temperature, while daytime heat alone had no significant effect. The leading explanation is that warm nights keep the plant’s metabolism running in the dark, burning through the sugars it stored during the day before they can be committed to grain.

blocks.zh: 農作一直是一種回應的實作：農友看到枯萎、變色或土壤乾裂，就出手處理。這套模式假設逆境會留下看得見的痕跡，而且來得及反應。夜溫上升推翻了這個假設。國際稻米研究所位於菲律賓的農場留下的 25 年紀錄（Peng et al., 2004）顯示，1979 到 2003 年間，夜間最低溫上升的速度大約是日間最高溫的三倍；夜溫每上升 1°C，乾季的穀粒產量就下降約 10%，而單獨的日間高溫並沒有顯著影響。目前主要的解釋是：溫暖的夜晚讓植物的代謝在黑暗中持續運轉，把白天儲存的糖分在能夠送進穀粒之前就燒掉。

blocks.en: What matters most here is not the size of that loss but its timing. The damage happens overnight, leaves the canopy looking entirely healthy by sunrise, and only becomes visible weeks later as a lighter harvest. A run of warm nights during grain filling can cost a season’s yield one year and miss the critical window entirely the next, so there is no reliable signal to watch for and no point at which a farmer could have stepped in. Even an attentive, experienced farmer cannot respond to stress that happens on the plant’s schedule rather than their own. As warming makes these events more frequent and less predictable, protection that waits for symptoms will increasingly arrive too late.

blocks.en: Taiwan’s geographical and climate variability arguably makes the island’s farmers more vulnerable to agricultural stress. Taiwan is barely 400 kilometers long, yet it holds both a tropical and a subtropical climate. A three-hour drive crosses a temperature range of roughly 19ºC.

blocks.zh: 臺灣的地理與氣候變異，可以說讓島上的農友更容易受到農業逆境的衝擊。臺灣長度不過 400 公里，卻同時擁有熱帶與副熱帶氣候。開三小時的車，就會跨越大約 19ºC 的溫差。

blocks.en: The underlying fragmentation innate to Taiwan is now colliding with a warming rate that continues to outpace tradition’s ability to adapt. For nearly a century, Taiwan’s average temperature crept upward by around 0.11ºC per decade – slow enough that a farmer could spend a lifetime farming and barely notice. Since 1991, that rate has nearly tripled to 0.29ºC per decade, with 2024 becoming Taiwan’s hottest year on record, with Taipei logging 63 days above 35ºC. Refer to Figure 3 for visualized crop yield changes in response to increasing heat stress.

blocks.en: When asked how she prepares for the dry season, Ms. Chen described layering dried weeds across her soil so morning dew soaked slowly into the ground, carrying her plants up to three weeks between checks. It is a schedule calibrated over decades on one plot of land, and it assumes stress will build at the pace it always has. Contrary to the certainty, a 2022 global study led by Hong Kong Polytechnic University found roughly 34-46% of flash droughts reached drought conditions within five days, with that share rising over 2000–2020 while frequency mostly held steady. Farmers’ knowledge hasn’t changed, but the window it was built for has shrunk. Closing that gap means protection already in place before stress arrives.

blocks.zh: 被問到如何因應乾季時，Chen 女士描述她會把乾枯的雜草層層鋪在土壤上，讓清晨的露水慢慢滲入地裡，讓作物在兩次巡田之間最多能撐三週。這是在同一塊地上用數十年校準出來的節奏，而它假設逆境會以一向的速度累積。與這份篤定相反，2022 年一項由香港理工大學主持的全球研究發現，大約 34-46% 的驟旱在五天之內就達到乾旱條件，而且這個比例在 2000–2020 年間上升，發生頻率則大致持平。農友的知識沒有改變，但這套知識所依據的時間窗已經縮短。要補上這道落差，意味著保護必須在逆境到來之前就已經就位。

blocks.en: Taiwan, at just 36 200 square kilometers, consumes more than 300 kilograms of fertilizer per hectare – compared to roughly 128 kilograms per hectare in the United States, a country 9.83 million square kilometers in size (Refer to Figure 6 and Figure 7). Part of this gap comes down to spatial pressure: only about a quarter of Taiwan’s land is viable for agriculture, versus roughly two-fifths in the US. But fertilizer use scaled to compensate for land scarcity comes at a cost. While fertilizer has propped up yields, excessive application strains underground soil biology and degrades soil quality over time.

blocks.en: That centralization problem isn't just chemical — it's logistical. To quantify it, we built a nationwide GIS routing model connecting every one of Taiwan's 613 registered fertilizer companies to real farmland (Refer to Figure 8): 2 792 536 individual parcels, aggregated by township into 346 demand nodes covering roughly 743 500 hectares of arable land. Each company is routed only to farmland inside its own county, using road-network distance rather than straight-line distance — the model won't let a company shortcut to a closer field across a county line, because that's not how actual distribution works.

blocks.en: Even under this best-case, same-county assumption, the model shows that centralized fertilizer production still has to travel: every kilogram makes a real trip along real roads before it reaches a real field, adding cost for time and emissions that a farm averaging under 1.1 hectares absorbs disproportionately relative to its output. A production model that instead manufactures the protectant on-site — at the scale of a single farm or a shared township reactor — removes that shipping step entirely.

blocks.en: In consideration to confirming and quantitatively measuring on-site on-demand deployment in fields, a highly important factor to consider is how well our engineered bacteria responds to light, how quickly is the response, and how much protectant is ultimately produced. The light plate apparatus (LPA) allows for quantitative analysis and accurate measurement rather than blindly answering these concerns qualitatively.
blocks.text: In consideration to confirming and quantitatively measuring on-site on-demand deployment in fields, a highly important factor to consider is how well our engineered bacteria responds to light, how quickly is the response, and how much protectant is ultimately produced. The light plate apparatus (LPA) allows for quantitative analysis and accurate measurement rather than blindly answering these concerns qualitatively.
blocks.zh: 要確認並定量量測田間的現地、隨需佈設，一個極為重要的因素是我們的工程菌對光的反應有多好、反應有多快，以及最終產出多少保護劑。光照板裝置（light plate apparatus, LPA）讓我們能做定量分析與準確量測，而不是只憑定性描述含糊地回答這些疑問。

blocks.en: The LPA is a 24-tube LED array that holds engineered Bacillus subtilis WB800 (CcaS/CcaR system) under six defined light conditions at once: green light (~535 nm) induces protectant production, and red light (~670 nm) halts it. Each condition is one column of four resistance-matched LEDs lighting four tubes. Intensity is set by Arduino PWM through three MOSFETs, one per tier (low, mid, high), and held constant for the whole run. Rather than a single endpoint reading, we sample each condition over time and track protectant output across the full period.

blocks.en: The production rate from the LPA is a direct input to Stage 2 of the Math Modeling sector (DryLab × GIS). There, it converts specific enzyme activities into a volumetric production rate. blocks.en: Chlorophyll degradation is one of the earliest and most reliable indicators of salt stress in plants. Sodium accumulation disrupts chloroplast structure, accelerates chlorophyll breakdown, and suppresses photosynthetic capacity well before visible wilting occurs. Thus, chlorophyll content serves as a quantitative proxy for stress damage, and by extension, for protectant efficacy. A plant that retains more chlorophyll under identical salt exposure is a plant that is better protected.

blocks.en: The GIS page ends with a number: what percentage of farmers’ yield can we retrieve from the effect of heat and salinity stresses. Human Practices asks the four questions that decide whether that number ever becomes hardware standing in a field: is it legal, who holds the capital, what does it cost against what the crop is worth, and is it actually better than what the farmer does/ has today. blocks.en: The Nantou farmer’s response to any proposed treatment was specific and immediate: a natural protectant would be acceptable, provided its compatibility with organic certification requirements could be confirmed. This farm is in the process of transitioning to certified organic status, and any input under consideration must remain compatible with that transition. This has direct implications for product positioning: a biological, GMO-derived treatment from our engineered bacteria such as ACC-deaminase is not merely acceptable to this segment of farmers but may represent the only category of input such farmers are willing to consider. This also identifies a concrete requirement for market entry, as confirming compatibility with organic certification standards is not a clean line, rather a gray area, making farmers in their trial stage of the organic transition unwilling to risk it and try out the product.

blocks.en: Taiwan’s tomato industry covers over 4000 hectares of farmland in Taiwan and is concentrated within a few counties. According to the Agricultural Knowledge Retrieval Platform, farmers harvested across 3627.94 hectares, yielding approximately 83.27 million kilograms in total, averaging 22 953 kg per hectare. blocks.en: As previously mentioned, Raster data and vector data are the most common and fundamental data types utilized within QGIS, one covering pixels, and the other utilizing lines/ points. Raster data sets are discrete and continuous cells (pixels) that represent data that gradually varies across space, also classifying them into different categories. Oftentimes, Raster data is used to present temperature or elevation maps as they can be visualized as continuous and gradient-like. Conversely, Vector data are scalable values that only depict discrete features like data points or lines; they are most commonly used to establish borders or outlines of files.

blocks.en: When researching global geospatial data, running into data sets with hundreds to thousands of numerics is inevitable. Oftentimes, these data sets are unorganized and condensed with tons of information, and they come in formats QGIS does not support, with field types that are inconsistent from row to row, no geometry column, or a non-standard text encoding, so QGIS cannot read them directly. Moreover with varying coordinate systems, data from different sources may have varying coordinates, unaligning in the software. Manually reconstructing thousands of numerics is time-consuming and could contain operator error, especially for students unfamiliar or non-professionals of the GIS field.

blocks.en: To address the following, we developed a broad, reusable prompt that generates data files in formats that QGIS is able to properly analyze (GeoJSON, CSV, SHP) from arbitrary raw input data. The following prompt, rather than being hard-wired to only analyze data sets beneficial to our project (Taiwan Farmland and Climate Volatility), the prompt is generalized so that any team desirable of use Geospatial Analyses can adapt it to develop their own geographic data set.

blocks.en: Our prompt, presented in Text 1, demonstrates that rules are grounded in established prompt engineering research rather than built ad hoc. Restricting the model to only use provided data reflects grounding research, shown to reduce hallucination (Addlesee, 2024). Flagging missing, ambiguous, or unusable values instead of guessing reflects calibration and abstention research, addressing a known tendency of LLMs to answer confidently rather than admit uncertainty. Requiring transparent calculation logic follows chain-of-thought prompting, shown to improve accuracy on multi-step tasks (Wei et al., 2022). Detecting and stating the coordinate reference system before use follows self-verification prompting, where an assumption is externalized so it can be checked rather than embedded silently in the output. Finally, requiring the output to exactly match the requested format (CSV, SHP, or GeoJSON) reflects structured output practices common to established frameworks such as CO-STAR and RTF, which produce more consistent, usable results than open-ended formatting instructions.

attrs.en: Geospatial Analysis. A team member points at a projected map of Taiwan's 2025 rice harvest by county.
Animated world map of projected irrigated rice yield from 2006 to 2098, green for high yield and red for low, with the high-yield belt shrinking over the century.
Ms. Chen crouching in a sunlit field beside a harvest basket, talking to two ReLEAF students who are crouched on either side of her, all three looking down at a patch of bare dark soil between them.

Map of Taiwan titled High Soil Variability: there are 12 USDA soil orders, Taiwan has 11. Soil series are coloured over satellite imagery, from clay loam through loam, sandy loam and silt loam to silty clay, changing colour every few kilometres down the western plain.
Two animated county maps of Taiwan side by side, year by year from 1980 to 2026: warming at each weather station since 1980 on the left, change in rice-growing area relative to 2005 on the right.

Map of Taiwan titled Correlation Between Average Age of Farmers in Taiwan and Amount of Heat Stress Experienced. Counties are shaded by average farmer age in 2016, from 55 years in pale yellow to 61 and over in dark blue, overlaid with dark red circles at weather stations sized by temperature change from 1991 to 2020.

Portrait map of Taiwan titled Taiwan Farmland Distribution x Climate Volatility, with counties shaded by climate volatility index from dark blue at 0.38 to yellow at 0.93, overprinted with farmland parcels in red where under 2 hectares and blue where above. Red parcels dominate the western plain.
World choropleth of fertilizer consumption in kilograms per hectare, pale pink to near-black, with an inset circle enlarging Taiwan in the darkest class alongside China, Japan and Malaysia.

Map of Taiwan titled 2024 Tomato Production in Taiwan Counties (kg), counties shaded from near white at 0 to 23,263 kg to near black at 10,714,006 to 17,185,322 kg. Chiayi is darkest, with Yunlin, Tainan and Kaohsiung labelled and nearly as dark down the south-west; the north and east are pale.

Map of Taiwan titled Change in Nov–Dec minimum temperature (°C), counties shaded from pale yellow at 0 to 1.0 °C warmer to dark red at 1.9 to 2.05 °C. Miaoli, Taichung, Nantou, Chiayi, Tainan and Kaohsiung are dark red; Yunlin, Changhua, Yilan, Hsinchu and Kinmen are red; the east coast, Pingtung and New Taipei are orange; Penghu is lightest.

Diagram in three columns. Input: user prompt or question, spatial file (CSV, SHP, GeoJSON), desired file formatting, desired file inclusion, destination platform. Interface: chat box, upload, table or chart display. Backend: data fabrication prevention, coordinate extraction and CRS detection, explicit uncertainty flagging, prioritize data validity, calculation logic exhibition, format matching.

Flow chart. The same data set of 15,138 rows and the same question go to a structured prompt and to a plain-language prompt. The structured prompt checks coordinate range and CRS, flags a coordinate precision issue (only 3,739 unique points), applies the filter and returns 2,502 rows. The plain-language prompt only checks for missing values, applies no filter and returns all 15,138 rows.
Two spreadsheet excerpts side by side, headed Structured Broad Prompt and Plain Language Prompt, with columns latitude, longitude, pH, app richness, two-class vegetation and EX kg/ha.
